description: Microsoft runs two parallel hiring tracks: the standardized Hiring Event (HE) loop covering Azure, Cloud, Copilot, and Office orgs, and Mustafa Suleyman's MAI org with its own recruiter pool and a distinctly OpenAI-flavored coding rotation. The HE bar is consistent — four 60-minute rounds back-to-back on a fixed weekday — with medium-difficulty algorithms and one system-design slot; MAI loops add project deep-dive depth and pull problems from an in-memory-DB / beam-search / streaming-decoder pool that does not overlap with classic LeetCode prep.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: LRU Cache (LC 146) + Multithreading Variant
questions.overview: Microsoft's most repeated cache implementation prompt: O(1) get/put on a bounded cache, with follow-ups spanning thread safety, TTL, LFU, and cross-machine sharding.

questions.title: In-Memory SQL Engine
questions.overview: Build a single-table in-memory database supporting SELECT, WHERE, and ORDER BY in 4-5 escalating follow-ups. CSV string is the initialization input; you write the parser too.

questions.title: DNA Shotgun Sequencing
questions.overview: Reconstruct a DNA string from fragments tagged at both ends. Three-part: ordered chain → undirected chain (Eulerian path) → multi-chain decomposition. The signature MAI "platform" coding problem.

questions.title: Delete and Earn (LC 740)
questions.overview: Maximize points by choosing values from an integer array: taking a value earns its points and removes values one smaller or one larger. The OA prompt “Maximize Score” is unchanged LC 740.

questions.title: Count Binary Substrings (LC 696)
questions.overview: Count contiguous binary substrings with equal numbers of zeros and ones, with each digit grouped consecutively. The intern OA uses the unchanged LC 696 problem under a renamed prompt.

questions.title: Alien Dictionary (LC 269)
questions.overview: The live-coding prompt was confirmed as LC 269: infer a valid character order from words already sorted in an alien language, return any valid ordering, and return an empty string when the ordering is invalid.

questions.title: Multi-Key Bounded Task Executor
questions.overview: Implement a thread-safe task executor that preserves submission order within each key, runs different keys concurrently under a global limit, bounds queued plus in-flight work, and shuts down gracefully with a timeout.

questions.title: Spiral Matrix (LC 54) + Follow-Ups
questions.overview: Traverse a 2-D matrix in clockwise spiral order and return the values as a one-dimensional sequence. Follow-ups switch to counterclockwise traversal and to filling an n × n matrix in spiral order.

questions.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal (LC 103)
questions.overview: Return a binary tree's values level by level, alternating left-to-right and right-to-left order on successive levels. The follow-up asks for a formulation using two alternating stacks.

questions.title: Palindrome Linked List (LC 234) + Engineering Follow-Up
questions.overview: Determine whether a singly linked list is a palindrome using O(1) auxiliary space. The follow-up requires restoring the list to its original structure before returning.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor (LC 235) with a Follow-Up Variant
questions.overview: Start with LC 235 and find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary search tree. The follow-up removes the BST ordering guarantee and becomes the general binary-tree problem in LC 236.

questions.title: Contiguous Memory Allocator
questions.overview: MAI / Copilot phone-screen coding: implement a fixed-size contiguous memory pool supporting allocate-by-size and free-a-region, then defend your allocation strategy.

questions.title: Tiny Next-Token Prediction Model (PyTorch Fill-In)
questions.overview: MSR Senior Researcher take-home-style live round: fill in TODOs in a tiny PyTorch repo — DataLoader, model layers, forward, training loop, next-token input/target preparation.

questions.title: SFT Sample Packing
questions.overview: Implement supervised fine-tuning sample packing: greedily pack variable-length (prompt, answer) pairs into fixed-length training sequences, emit per-token loss masks aligned to answer positions only, and balance sequence usage across the batch.

questions.title: Sliding-Window Stream Session Bucketing
questions.overview: Azure phone screen. Given a stream of timestamped events, return the (min, max) of each fixed-width time bucket in a single O(N) pass.

questions.title: In-Place Sub-Matrix Move
questions.overview: Given a large matrix and the coordinates of a smaller embedded sub-matrix, move the sub-matrix to a new location within the larger matrix — in-place — handling overlap correctly.

questions.title: KV Store with Snapshot Versions
questions.overview: Build an in-memory KV store that supports point-in-time snapshots, reads scoped to a snapshot id, and writes that branch from a snapshot without polluting earlier snapshots.

questions.title: Beam Search Decoder Implementation
questions.overview: Implement beam search decoding for a language model — greedy first, then top-K beam expansion. The neural network is stubbed; you only own the decoding logic and the beam bookkeeping.

questions.title: Gen / Score Task Lock Scheduler
questions.overview: Implement a `TaskLock` so that a pool of `gen` and `score` tasks executes in parallel but `score` tasks of a given id only run after their matching `gen` task completes. Pure Python threading.

questions.title: Multiply Strings (LC 43)
questions.overview: Classic big-integer multiplication on string inputs without using built-in big-int types. HE coding round; complexity follow-up is expected.

questions.title: Parse Email Addresses from a Log String
questions.overview: Single-pass character scanner over a long log string with `;`-separated email records. Each record may have an optional display name and comments anywhere; deduplicate and return the list of emails.

questions.title: 15-Puzzle Minimum Moves (BFS)
questions.overview: Given a 4×4 sliding tile puzzle state, return the minimum number of moves to reach the solved configuration (or `-1` if unreachable). Pure BFS on a state graph.

questions.title: Idempotency API with Idempotency-Key Header
questions.overview: HE round opener: design and implement an API endpoint that deduplicates retries via an `Idempotency-Key` header. The interviewer hands you a spec sheet and watches whether you cover replay semantics, concurrent in-flight retries, and TTL eviction.

questions.title: Distance from Each Node to the Cycle in an Undirected Graph
questions.overview: Given an undirected graph that contains exactly one cycle, return for every node its shortest distance to any node on the cycle. Cycle nodes return 0.

questions.title: Sort 0..32000 with Bit-Vector Storage
questions.overview: Classic Bell Labs / Bentley problem revived for an Azure storage HM round. Sort an unsorted, duplicate-free integer file with values in [0, 32000] using only `getNum()` / `putNum()` helpers — and minimal memory.

questions.title: Validate Lat/Long With Minimum Expensive API Calls
questions.overview: Process a multi-million-row CSV of store locations; for each row, verify that the stored (lat, long) matches the geocoded version of its address. The geocoding API is expensive — minimize the number of calls.

questions.title: Maximum-Value Frequency in Array Suffixes
questions.overview: Given `nums` and query indices, return for each index how many times the maximum value of that suffix appears. Two independent MAI interviews used the same example and contract.

questions.title: Merge Intervals (LC 56) + Interview Variant
questions.overview: The canonical prompt is LC 56: sort intervals by start and merge overlaps into disjoint ranges. A Hiring Event variant instead asks for the original intervals that participate in any overlap, so clarify the expected output before coding.

questions.title: Minimum Fuel Cost Across a Road Network
questions.overview: In a 90-minute Microsoft OA, minimize the cost to travel from A to B in an undirected weighted road network where each city sells fuel at a different price and vehicles have unlimited capacity. Return -1 when B is unreachable; the prompt supplies a complete getMinCost contract and a five-city example.

questions.title: Top-K Largest Elements (Retain / Rank Stores)
questions.overview: The recurring MAI phone-screen coding warm-up: return the top-K elements of a list under a simple ranking rule. It appears as direct top-K selection, retaining the K largest in original order, or ranking business candidates by a composite key.

questions.title: Org Chart Report Count (Tree Aggregation)
questions.overview: Given a manager → reports graph, answer `countReports(id)` quickly under read-heavy workloads. Follow-up: how to update the aggregate when a single relationship changes.

questions.title: Balanced Permutation Prefix Check
questions.overview: OA prompt also seen on Uber. For each k in [1..n], decide whether some contiguous subarray of permutation p contains exactly the multiset {1..k}. Return a binary string.

questions.title: Count Positive Pairs Satisfying 1/x + 1/y = 1/N
questions.overview: HackerRank OA staple branded "Equations". Given N ≤ 10⁶, count ordered positive-integer pairs (x, y) with 1/x + 1/y = 1/N. The naive scan TLEs; the right answer reduces to a divisor count.

questions.title: Resumable Batch Dataloader with Weighted Sampling
questions.overview: Build an iterator over a multi-source dataset that supports checkpointable resume, mixed batching by source weight, and weights that don't divide the batch size cleanly.

questions.title: Streaming Stop-Token Detection
questions.overview: Decode an LLM token stream and stop emission the instant a forbidden stop sequence appears — including when the stop sequence straddles chunk boundaries. No full-stream buffering allowed.

questions.title: Hand-Written K-Means
questions.overview: Implement K-Means from scratch in numpy / PyTorch / plain Python. The HM phone screen for Applied Scientist 2 routinely opens with this; sometimes followed by a time-complexity discussion.

questions.title: Palindrome Number + Next-Greater Palindrome
questions.overview: Two-part HE coding round. First: detect whether an integer is a palindrome without converting to a string. Second: find the smallest palindrome strictly greater than the input.

questions.title: Rate Limiter (Design + Implementation)
questions.overview: Recurring Microsoft prompt that crosses categories. Some loops ask for a 30-minute coding implementation, others for a full system-design treatment, and one HE pairs both in the same round. Scale follow-up converges on 100K QPS.

questions.title: Todo List Full-Stack System Design
questions.overview: Design a todo-list application with create-list, task CRUD, viewing, ordering, authentication / authorization, cache behavior, API versioning, service-to-service auth, and a 500 requests-per-second user-load follow-up.

questions.title: Chatbot Personalization / Memory System Design
questions.overview: MAI / Copilot onsite system design: design the long-term memory and personalization layer behind a text chatbot — how to store, retrieve, and reconcile per-user history so responses are personalized without re-reading everything each turn.

questions.title: Distributed Web Crawler System Design
questions.overview: MAI phone-screen SD slot. 30-minute compressed treatment — get the pipeline shape, politeness, and dedup right before time runs out.

questions.title: Search Autocomplete / Typeahead System Design
questions.overview: MAI VO SD slot. Design a low-latency prefix-search service that powers a search bar's typeahead suggestions.

questions.title: Job Scheduler / ETL Pipeline System Design
questions.overview: HE SD slot. Design a system that schedules and executes long-running ETL jobs reliably, with retry and dependency semantics.

questions.title: URL Shortener / Tiny URL System Design
questions.overview: Recurring HE / VO / phone-screen prompt. Variants now include vanilla HLD, a higher-scale write-spike design, and a compressed HLD + LLD round where working HackerRank code and AI-generated-code bug review are expected.

questions.title: Ticket Booking / Ticketmaster System Design
questions.overview: Azure / Office VO SD prompt. The core question is seat-locking under concurrency for high-traffic event drops.

questions.title: Behavioral Round (Growth Mindset / Customer Obsession)
questions.overview: Behavioral questions appear inside coding rounds and in standalone HM or AA rounds. Microsoft's value-driven prompts cluster around growth mindset, collaboration, ownership, judgment, and technical decision-making.

questions.title: Project Deep Dive
questions.overview: Mandatory across MAI and most traditional loops. 30-60 minutes of unstructured drilling on one project the candidate picks. Interviewers probe ownership, decision rationale, and what would change in hindsight.

questions.title: Object-Oriented Design Round
questions.overview: Specifically a Microsoft staple. Some Azure loops replace one coding round with an explicit OOD prompt — design class hierarchies, interfaces, and inheritance relationships for a small system in code.

questions.title: Transformer Roofline + FP32→FP16 Drill
questions.overview: MAI AI-infra loop: read transformer code, compute matmul wall-clock from roofline, vibe-code CUDA in your own editor, then defend the residual-connection gradient path under FP32→FP16 casting.
